html:
The Taku River Tlingit are an inland branch of the Tlingit people, living around Atlin Lake in far northern British Columbia and in the southern Yukon. Most Tlingit live on the coast of southeast Alaska; these groups moved inland along the Taku River, the main trade route between the coast and the interior, and married into the local Athabaskan peoples such as the Tagish.

They carried coastal goods such as eulachon oil inland and brought furs back. The Klondike rush and a gold rush at Atlin in 1898 flooded their land with miners. The Teslin Tlingit are close relatives. In 2004 the Supreme Court of Canada ruled in their case over a mining road that governments must consult First Nations before such projects, a key decision in Canadian law.
